literal: Virtue it will yield, happiness and it will yield, proper means having known, evil without, that came wealth.
translation: Wealth acquired through proper means and without doing evil will yield both virtue and happiness.
modern: சரியான வழியை அறிந்து தீமை இல்லாமல் சேர்க்கப்பட்ட செல்வம் ஒருவனுக்கு அறத்தையும் தரும் இன்பத்தையும் தரும்.
explanation: This couplet explains the dual benefits of wealth earned righteously. When a person accumulates wealth by knowing the proper methods and avoiding evil deeds, that wealth becomes a source of good. It yields virtue because it can be used for righteous deeds, and it yields happiness by providing a good life free from guilt. The repetition of the word yield emphasizes that both outcomes naturally flow from pure wealth.
